docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ## 2. Order of operations for a new project
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
## 2. Order of operations for a new project

Run these from the project root (it must be a git repository; `fgctl init`
refuses outside one).

1. Install `fgctl` once per machine:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vantt/forgent/main/install.sh | sh
   ```

   It downloads `fgctl-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` from the release, verifies it
   against `SHA256SUMS`, and puts `fgctl` in `~/.local/bin` (override with
   `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR`). If `~/.local/bin` is not on `PATH` it tells you what to
   export. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` are supported; on Windows use `install.ps1` from PowerShell instead (see the README Install section).

2. Activate fgOS in the project with `fgctl init`. Where the release comes
   from, first match wins: `--from <path|URL>`, then `FGCTL_FROM`, then
   `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, then the release pinned by the project's committed
   `.fgos/distribution.json`, then the latest GitHub release. For a first
   install nothing needs downloading by hand:

   ```bash
   fgctl init                              # no pin: downloads the latest release
   FGCTL_VERSION=v0.2.0-rc.1 fgctl init    # an exact tag (pre-releases are never "latest")
   FGCTL_FROM=./fgos-<tag>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz fgctl init   # a non-release build
   ```

   A download goes through `curl` and is verified against the release's
   `SHA256SUMS`: a missing or mismatching entry stops the init before anything
   is staged. A URL given to `--from`/`FGCTL_FROM` must have a `SHA256SUMS` next
   to it; a local path is used as is. `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` points downloads at
   a mirror. A download records its tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`
   (`projectRuntime.releaseVersion`); a teammate's plain `fgctl init` on a
   machine without that release then downloads the same tag and refuses if its
   digest is not the pinned one. A pin without a tag (digest only) still needs
   one of the sources above on such a machine. The `curl-available` doctor check reports a missing `curl`.

   `fgctl init` stages the release into the machine store, writes
   `.fgos/installation/`, and then, using the new shim, runs this tail in order:

   ```text
   .fgos/installation/bin/fgos init
   .fgos/installation/bin/fgos doctor --fix
   .fgos/installation/bin/fgos doctor
   ```

   If any tail command exits non-zero, `fgctl init` exits non-zero and the
   install is recorded as `ready-degraded`. Note that `fgos doctor` exits 0
   even when checks fail (see section 3; `--strict` changes that, but the tail
   does not use it), so a green `fgctl init` does not mean a green doctor.

3. Read the doctor report yourself and clear everything the tool could not fix
   (section 4 says which is which):

   ```bash
   .fgos/installation/bin/fgos doctor --pretty
   ```

4. Do the owner steps in section 5 (trust in every agent CLI home, pools with
   enough provider families). No tool writes those for you.

5. If config defaults or hooks are still reported as missing (the
   `... -- run fgos setup` messages), run the legacy `fgos setup` once:

   ```bash
   .fgos/installation/bin/fgos setup
   ```

   See "What setup still does that doctor --fix does not" below.

Later, to move the project to a newer release:

```bash
fgctl upgrade
# or a specific tag / local archive:
FGCTL_VERSION=v0.2.0 fgctl upgrade
fgctl upgrade --from ./fgos-<new-version>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
```

`fgctl upgrade` downloads and verifies the release when no `--from` is given, updates `.fgos/distribution.json` (recording the tag when downloaded), and records the previous release so `fgctl repair` can roll back.
Check what is active with `fgctl status` (`--json` for machines).

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 2.1. What each command does
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 2.1. What each command does

| Command | Does | Writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `install.sh` | Installs the `fgctl` binary | `~/.local/bin/fgctl` |
| `fgctl stage --from <release>` | Puts a release into the machine store without activating it | machine store |
| `fgctl init [--from <release or URL>]` | Downloads the release when none is given or pinned, stages (if needed), activates in this project, runs the init/doctor tail | `.fgos/installation/`, machine store |
| `fgctl upgrade [--from <release or URL>]` | Downloads the latest or `FGCTL_VERSION` release when none is given, moves the project to it, updates `.fgos/distribution.json`, keeps the previous release, runs the tail | `.fgos/installation/`, `.fgos/distribution.json`, machine store |
| `fgctl repair` | Rolls back to the previous release if one is recorded, otherwise re-verifies and re-publishes the same one | `.fgos/installation/` |
| `fgctl verify` | Verifies the active release's files against its manifest and quarantines it on drift | quarantine on failure |
| `fgctl status` | Shows the active and previous release and staged releases | nothing |
| `fgos init` | Creates the `.fgos/` store (event log, empty view, coexistence manifest) | `.fgos/` |
| `fgos doctor` | Runs every check and reports | nothing |
| `fgos doctor --fix` | Runs every registered fix, then reports the checks again | the fixes listed in section 4 |
| `fgos doctor --strict` | Same report; exits 1 when any check fails (also with `--fix`) | nothing |
| `fgos setup` | Legacy. Wires shell integration, fills config defaults, wires git and Claude Code hooks, runs every registered fix, materializes skills | project and global config, rc files, hooks |

If the shim says `no active runtime -- run fgctl init` or
`active runtime is not ready (...) -- run fgctl repair`, do what it says.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 2.2. What setup still does that doctor --fix does not

`fgos setup` is marked deprecated, but `fgctl init`, then `fgos doctor --fix`,
then `fgos doctor` does not fill the config defaults. `doctor --fix` only runs
the fixes in section 4; the check messages for missing config sections, the git
hook and the Claude Code dispatch hook all still say "run fgos setup", and only
`setup` writes them (its help now says so too). Run `fgos setup` once in the
project when those checks are red. It never overwrites a value you already set.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ## 3. Reading doctor output
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
## 3. Reading doctor output

```bash
fgos doctor --pretty    # one line per check, a tick or a cross
fgos doctor --json      # {"data": {"checks": [{id, description, passed, message}]}}
fgos doctor --fix --json   # adds data.fixed: [{id, changed, message}] and re-reports checks
```

- Plain `doctor` and `doctor --fix` both exit 0 whatever the checks say: the
  `fgctl init|upgrade|repair` tail runs them and treats a non-zero exit as a
  degraded install, and a project that has not run `fgos setup` always has red
  checks. Read `passed`, or pass `--strict` (`fgos doctor --strict`,
  `fgos doctor --fix --strict`) to get exit 1 when any check fails, for scripts
  and CI. A check that reports `passed: true` with an "informational" note never
  trips `--strict`.
- A check that cannot be evaluated here (no runner config, not a fgOS checkout,
  nothing to check) reports `passed: true` with a "not applicable" or "nothing
  to check" message. A green line is not always a proof, read the message.
- `--fix` only runs the fixes that are registered (section 4). Anything else it
  leaves alone and the check stays red.
- `fgos doctor` resolves the project from where you run it (from a linked
  worktree it resolves the main checkout). Run it from inside the project.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
## 4. Every doctor check

Who fixes it:

- **tool**: `fgos doctor --fix` repairs it.
- **setup**: `fgos setup` repairs it (and `doctor --fix` does not).
- **you**: only the project owner can, by hand. fgOS never edits those files.
- **info**: informational, or only reports. No action required unless you care.

The registered checks below come from `src/setup/registrations.mjs`
(`src/setup/checks.mjs` re-exports it). Some read-only checks list the failing
file or key in their message; the message always names the exact target.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 4.1. Machine and installation
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.1. Machine and installation

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node-version-and-git` | Node 18 or newer and git on `PATH` | `node v16.x -- need >=18` | you | Install Node 18+ or git |
| `cli-version-visible` | `fgos version` resolves this build's version and verbs | `fgos version did not resolve a packageVersion...` | you | No fix is registered: repair the runtime (`fgctl repair`) or reinstall |
| `shell-integration-sourced` | The shell-integration `source` line is in your rc files and the `fgos` function really works | `not sourced in: ~/.zshrc -- run fgos setup`; `sourced correctly, but "fgos --help" fails after stripping ...` (shown as an informational, still passing, note when doctor runs inside an agent harness shell) | setup, you | `fgos setup` adds the line. Dead `source` lines it reports must be deleted by hand. Open a new shell. The "fails after stripping" form is a harness shell snapshot dropping a helper, not a project problem; run doctor from your own terminal to see the real verdict. Only relevant to dev checkouts |
| `plugin-skill-cli-reachable` | A `fgos` CLI is reachable from this project (workspace installation, local `bin/fgos.mjs`, project-local install, or global `PATH`) | `no bin/fgos.mjs at <cwd>, no project-local node_modules/.bin/fgos, and no global fgos install on PATH -- every /fgOS:* slash command will fail on first use` | you | `fgctl init` in the project (its message still names the legacy `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent`) |
| `bin-discovery-cache` | (fix only, no check) refreshes the cached global `fgos` path | none | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `rust-host-binary-present` | The active release's `bin/fgos` exists and is executable | `no active fgos rust host release or dev checkout found` | you | `fgctl repair` |
| `rust-host-target-supported` | The OS and CPU are an approved Rust host target | names the unsupported platform | you | Use `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` or `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; no other target is shipped |
| `legacy-node-payload-present` | The legacy Node payload named by the release manifest exists | `no active fgos rust host release or dev checkout found` | you | `fgctl repair` |
| `active-release-matches-checkout` | Activated Node payload matches doctor's source working tree; staged dependencies excluded | changed/missing/extra counts, up to five paths, digest and activation time | you | Use `npm run fgos:dev -- <verb>` for working-tree code, or rebuild/stage/upgrade to update plain `fgos`; no automatic fix. ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 4.2. Project config (written by setup or `--fix`)
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.2. Project config (written by setup or `--fix`)

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config-not-stale` | `.fgos/config.json` exists and has every current default key | `not yet configured -- run fgos setup`; `stale config -- missing keys: ...` | setup | `fgos setup` (only adds missing keys, never overwrites yours) |
| `runner-rigor-config` | `runner.rigorToTier` is complete in the project and global config | `project runner.rigorToTier missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup`; or fix the named key by hand |
| `runner-patterns-config` | `runner.patterns` is present, well formed and cumulative | `runner.patterns missing -- falling back to setup defaults` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `runner-generated-paths` | `runner.generatedPaths` maps a generated source to its render targets with well-formed write-scope entries | `runner.generatedPaths missing -- write scopes are not widened to generated trees` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `tier-vocabulary-dead-keys` | No retired tier keys (`runner.models`, `minTier`, `rigorOverrides`) | names the dead key | you | Delete or migrate the named key |
| `model-policy-tier-coverage` | `runner.modelPolicies` has a model for every tier `rigorToTier` produces, for every provider | `global provider "openai" missing model for tier "standard"` | you | Add the model for that provider and tier under `runner.modelPolicies` in the named config file |
| `executor-family-unique` | Each agent family has one executor | `one family, several executors: claude (claude, claude-herdr)` | you | Merge them: keep one executor and move the other's transports into it as invocations |
| `executor-skills-installed` | Every skill an executor declares in `supports.skills` exists in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout | `claude declares ak:cook but .claude/skills/ak-cook/SKILL.md is missing in /path/repo` | you | Install the skill for that runtime, or remove it from `executors.<id>.supports.skills` |
| `tier-fallback` | Every family `runner.tierFallback` lists for a tier has a `modelPolicies` cell at that tier and an agent executor | `warning: tier fallback entries the walk skips: advanced: z-ai has no modelPolicies cell at advanced` | you | Add the cell, or remove the family from that tier's list |
| `model-policy-pools` | Every pool a tier cell names (`model@pool`) has accounts in `runner.llmAccounts` (the walk skips an entry whose pool has none) | `warning: tier cells name pools runner.llmAccounts does not declare: deepseek.standard@openrouter; the walk skips these entries until the pool has an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI of the invocation (fgos dispatch explain shows each)` | you | Declare the pool's accounts under `runner.llmAccounts` in `~/.fgos/config.json` |
| `llm-accounts-shape` | `runner.llmAccounts` is in the global config only and well formed | `runner.llmAccounts.codex: "codex" is another spelling of the family "openai"` | you | Fix the named key in `~/.fgos/config.json` |
| `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` | `runner.llmAccounts` and `runner.providers` list the same accounts and login directories (the lease reads `runner.llmAccounts` for a pool it declares and `runner.providers` for the rest) | `warning: the lease reads runner.llmAccounts for a pool it declares and runner.providers for the rest; only in runner.providers: gemini/tetcu72` | you | Add the missing account to the side that lacks it |
| `capability-rigor-ceiling` | Which capabilities run above `runner.maxTier` because they declare a higher `rigor` themselves (informational) | `above runner.maxTier flagship by their own rigor: architecture:synthesize (rigor critical) runs at frontier: claude fable` | you | Lower that capability's `rigor` if the cost is not wanted |
| `global-model-policies-portable` | Global `runner.modelPolicies` uses plain model names | `~/.fgos/config.json runner.modelPolicies has list or "model@pool" cells (deepseek.standard)` | you | Move those cells to the project config |
| `advise-execute-capabilities-configured` | `runner.capabilities` declares `advise`, `execute`, `code:implement` | `runner.capabilities section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `workflow-capabilities-configured` | Every capability a Workflow unit names is declared, and has a `prefer` pool | `no entry for Workflow capabilities: ...`; `warning: ... no "prefer" pool, so a headless run of those units is refused` | setup, you | `fgos setup` declares the capabilities. The `prefer` pool is yours to fill (section 5.2) |
| `capability-serves-valid` | The `serves` sets are well formed, distinct and include `review` | `runner.capabilities section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `operation-capability-resolves` | Coordination operations' declared capabilities resolve against the config | `runner config section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `worker-slots-ceiling-usable` | `workerSlots.ceiling` is a positive integer or explicit `null` | `workerSlots section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup`; set an integer (8 is recommended) to enforce a ceiling |
| `invariant-checks-configured` | `invariantChecks.commands` has a runnable command | `invariantChecks section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup`, then put your project's own check command there |
| `worktree-setup-configured` | `worktreeSetup.commands` is a list of non-empty shell commands | names the bad entry | you | Edit `worktreeSetup.commands` |
| `gate-bypass-configured` | `gateBypass.level` is one of off, light, standard, heavy | `gateBypass.level missing or not a recognized level ... -- run fgos doctor --fix` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `iron-law-configured` | `ironLaw.level` is ask or warn | `ironLaw.level missing ... -- run fgos doctor --fix` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `gateway-token-configured` | `gateway.token` is present in `~/.fgos/config.json` | `gateway.token missing from ~/.fgos/config.json` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` (never rotates an existing token) |
| `herdr-launcher-configured` | `herdrOrchestrator` toggles are present booleans | `herdrOrchestrator section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `herdr-web-dashboard-configured` | `herdrWebDashboard.staticServing` is a boolean | `herdrWebDashboard section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `doc-registry-enforce` | `docRegistry.enforce` is a boolean | `docRegistry section missing -- run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `main-checkout-hook-wired` | `core.hooksPath` points at `.githooks` (the main-checkout lock hook) | `core.hooksPath not wired to .githooks ... run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` (never re-points a custom hooks path). Only meaningful when the project carries `.githooks` |
| `dispatch-decide-hook-wired` | `.claude/settings.json` has the PreToolUse hook that forces `dispatch decide` before Agent/Task calls | `.claude/settings.json has no PreToolUse dispatch-decide hook wired ... run fgos setup` | setup | `fgos setup` |
| `instruction-projections-stale` | The effective instruction projections and ledger are current | `instruction projections not materialized -- run fgos doctor --fix` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sample: 4.3. Agent CLIs, trust and Workflow readiness
ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 4.3. Agent CLIs, trust and Workflow readiness
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.3. Agent CLIs, trust and Workflow readiness

These are the checks a project owner has to act on. Section 5 explains each
manual step.

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-cli-project-trusted` | The project root is trusted in every codex home and agy sub-HOME the configured executors use | `codex config ~/.codex-x/config.toml (openai) has no entry for /path; codex will stop at "Trust this folder?"`; `agy settings ... does not list /path in trustedWorkspaces` | you | codex: add `[projects."<root>"]` and `trust_level = "trusted"` to the named `config.toml`. agy: add the root to the `trustedWorkspaces` array in the named `settings.json`. fgOS never edits these files |
| `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` | For every reviewed Workflow unit, the `prefer` pool has a provider family different from the producer's; a panel pool with fewer families than seats is noted (seats share a family), not failed | `capability prefer pools cannot supply the independent provider families these Workflow units need: ...` | you | Add a `prefer` entry on another provider family under `runner.capabilities.<capability>` |
| `trust-store-readable` | Claude's folder-trust store `~/.claude.json` is readable and has a `projects` object, so fgOS can pre-trust its own worktrees | `trust store at ~/.claude.json is unreadable: ...` or `... is not valid JSON` or `... has no usable "projects" object` | you | Start `claude` once so it creates the file; fix its permissions or its content |
| `non-claude-trust-stores-readable` | Every codex or agy trust store named in an executor is readable | names the unreadable store | you | Fix the path in the executor config, or start that CLI once so the file exists |
| `confined-pane-accounts` | Every confined herdr invocation with a private home has an account whose credential files exist | `no runner.providers.z-ai.accounts in the global config, so its pane starts in an empty private home, logged out` | you | Add the account under `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` in `~/.fgos/config.json`, and log that CLI in |
| `agy-permissions-configured` | agy's `settings.json` has a working command denylist | the message says what the settings file lacks | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `agy-sub-homes-configured` | Each agy sub-HOME named by an executor has `toolPermission: always-proceed` | names the sub-HOME | tool, you | Re-run `fgos doctor --fix`; if it persists, edit that sub-HOME's `settings.json` |
| `tool-registry-configured` | Declared tool providers (such as an impact-analysis tool) are present on this machine | `degraded -- 1/2 registered tool(s) present (1 missing, ...) run fgos tool check` | you | Install the missing tool, then `fgos tool check` to refresh the local overlay |
| `provider-capacity-state` | Provider account leases and quarantine are reportable. Doctor never clears quarantine | `provider-capacity quarantine present (acct:quota-limit:until=...)` | you | Inspect with `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity`, fix the cause, then `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine` |
| `lock-kernel-semantics` | Both lock directories (`.fgos/locks`, `~/.local/state/fgos/locks`) give kernel lock exclusion, proven by a two-process probe | `... does not exist yet, not measured` (warning) or `... the filesystem gives no lock exclusion` | you | Run `fgos setup` for a missing directory; move the workspace or state root off a network filesystem |
| `lock-borrow-vectors` | A lock lent to a git child never leaks to a background process git starts | `borrowed lock leaks (git version ...): <vector>: <detail>` | you | Report it: activation refuses the same release; do not work around it |
| `lock-holders` | Every holder of an fgOS lock is an fgOS process or a borrowed child, and no previous holder's processes are left | `warning: gateway <path> held by pid <n> (<cmdline>), not a fgOS process ...` | you | Stop the named process; for a `predecessor.json` warning, confirm the domain is gone, then remove that record |
| `lock-fences` | Every legacy lock path carries its cutover fence, so an older fgOS binary fails loudly | `warning: N of M legacy lock path(s) not fenced ...` | tool | After activating this release, stop every fgOS process of the workspace and run `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` | `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` is an integer from 1 to 60000 | `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs = "2000" (project) must be an integer from 1 to 60000` | you | Fix the value in `.fgos/config.json` or `~/.fgos/config.json` |
| `state-root` | Node and the Rust host resolve the same state root | `Node and the host disagree: ...` | you | Run through the `fgos` command, or set `FGOS_HOST_BIN` to a host of the same release |
| `terminal-control` | The terminal driver (herdr) answers through the terminal port; prints its capabilities and the herdr server it talks to | `warning: terminal mode unsupported: herdr is not usable (herdr); direct mode unaffected` (a failure only for a bad `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE`) | you | Install herdr to use terminal mode; direct mode needs nothing |
| `terminal-config` | `terminal.*` settings pass their rules; prints each value and whether it came from the project, the global config or the default | `terminal.allocationGraceMs = 40000 must be an integer of at least 60000 ...` | you | Fix the value in `.fgos/config.json` or `~/.fgos/config.json` |
| `terminal-allocations` | No terminal slot is stuck past `terminal.allocationGraceMs` and no retained pane is past its time | `warning: 1 slot(s) need a person; nothing was closed: <key>: ...` | you | Close the named pane yourself; doctor never closes one |
| `herdr-executor-kinds` | Every executor dispatched through a herdr pane names a supported agent kind and no outdated integration hook | names the executor | you | Fix the executor's kind in the config |
| `executor-profile-warnings` | Legacy executor entries hardcoding policy-shaped flags or account-pool env | `9 legacy executor-profile warning(s) (informational, not blocking)` | info | Migrate when convenient; each item names the target |

| `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` | For every reviewed Workflow unit, the `prefer` pool has a provider family different from the producer's; a panel pool with fewer families than seats is noted (seats share a family), not failed | `capability prefer pools cannot supply the independent provider families these Workflow units need: ...` | you | Add a `prefer` entry on another provider family under `runner.capabilities.<capability>` |
| `trust-store-readable` | Claude's folder-trust store `~/.claude.json` is readable and has a `projects` object, so fgOS can pre-trust its own worktrees | `trust store at ~/.claude.json is unreadable: ...` or `... is not valid JSON` or `... has no usable "projects" object` | you | Start `claude` once so it creates the file; fix its permissions or its content |

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.4. Confinement

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `confinement-policies-declared` | Policies referenced by capabilities exist | names the unknown policy | you | Declare it under `runner.confinementPolicies` or fix the reference |
| `confinement-backend-registry-readable` | The machine registry `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` exists and is valid | `machine backend registry not found at ... -- run fgos doctor --fix` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` | No confinement temp dirs are left by a dead process | `1 empty per-dispatch dir(s) left behind across /tmp/fgos-confinement -- run "fgos doctor --fix"` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `confinement-bwrap-platform` | The bwrap backend in the machine registry is enabled and its executable verified | the message names the broken state | you | Install or enable bubblewrap; re-run |
| `confinement-probe-freshness` | The 8 confinement probes pass | names the failing probe | you | Fix the named probe's cause (usually bwrap or namespace permissions) |
| `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` | Every blind Workflow unit's capability pool can only bind executors whose provider family and transport were proven blind by the live canary (claude and xai through herdr, openai through herdr or cli, glm and deepseek through cli; gemini is not proven) | `blind steps can bind executors not proven to keep a worker blind: <workflow>/<step>/<unit>: <executor> via <invocation> ...`; passes as not applicable when no unit is blind | you | Remove that executor from the capability's `prefer` pool for the blind step, or run the canary for that family and transport and add a row to `BLIND_PROVEN_PAIRS` in `src/setup/blind-steps-proven-pools.mjs` |
| `confinement-blind-read` | A blind unit can be enforced (the bwrap backend hides peer run state from a worker) | `blind-read: fail (...)` names what the worker could still read; `backend-unsupported` means blind units are refused | you | Fix bwrap or namespace permissions, as for the probe row |
| `confinement-strict-readiness` | Strict confinement is possible (all capabilities have known policies, bwrap ready) | `warning: strict confinement disabled (capability "x" missing confinement policy ...)` | info | Declare a policy per capability if you want strict mode |
| `confinement-herdr-maturity` | Reports how far herdr confinement has converged | never fails | info | none |

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 4.5. Work state, git and coordination hygiene
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.5. Work state, git and coordination hygiene

Mostly relevant after the project has real work items.

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` | Every mutating assignment result matches its unit snapshot | `error scanning assignments` or a mismatch | you | Report it; do not edit the assignment files |
| `coordination-protocol-dead-vocabulary` | Coordination protocols and workflows do not use retired `minTier` / `minRigor` | names the file | you | Edit the named definition |
| `task-specs-resolve` | Every domain's task spec and every core task spec resolves to a real file | `missing task-spec file(s): coding.operations.discovery[judge-ambiguity] -> ... not found` | you | Resolved against the fgOS install doctor runs from, not the project, so a plain project without fgOS's own `domains/` and `core/` trees passes. A failure means the installed release itself is incomplete: run `fgctl repair` |
| `agent-claims-resolve` | Every agent type's claims name real task specs | names the unresolved claim | info | Same as above |
| `domain-registry-compiled` | Every domain's `compiled.json` exists and parses | `... -- run npm run build:domains` | you | In an fgOS source checkout, `npm run build:domains` |
| `agent-type-names-unique` | Agent type names are globally unique | names the duplicate | you | Rename one |
| `work-classification-vocabulary` | Open items' risk and kind match their domain's vocabulary | `N open item(s) outside their domain's classification` | you | Re-classify the named items |
| `work-step-vocabulary` | No open item is stranded on a retired step | `2 open item(s) at a step their domain no longer registers` | you | Drain the named items; no verb relabels a live item's step |
| `domain-workflow-operations-coverage` | Every Workflow step operation resolves to valid task specs, roles, skills and legal edges | `15 workflow step operation problem(s): ...` | you | Same root as `task-specs-resolve` (the fgOS install, not the project); a failure means the installed release is inconsistent |
| `root-drift` | No `fgw/<root>` branch is ahead of its target | `drifted root branch(es) need syncing: ... -- run fgos sync-root <root-id>` | you | `fgos sync-root <root-id>` |
| `leaf-notify-drift` | No live session branch has post-land drift | names the branch | you | Rebase or resync the named branch |
| `delivered-not-on-trunk` | Every handed-over item's branch is reachable from the trunk | names the item | you | Merge or catch up the named item |
| `events-jsonl-not-truncated` | `.fgos/events.jsonl` was not silently reverted by a stash, checkout, reset or clean | `truncation detected in events.jsonl, ...` | you | No fix is registered: stop writing to the store, restore the log from backup and find what reverted it |
| `events-compaction-verified` | Past `.fgos/events/` compactions still match their archives | names the compaction | you | Report it; do not delete archives |
| `main-checkout-guard-warnings` | The main-checkout guard log has no recorded regressions | `1300 main checkout guard warning(s) recorded` | info | Read the log named in the message; clear only after review |
| `no-stuck-merge-abort` | The main checkout has no lingering `MERGE_HEAD` | `merge in progress or stuck (MERGE_HEAD=...) -- run fgos main-checkout-reset ...` | you | `--fix` never acts here by design. Review `git status`, then `fgos main-checkout-reset --sha <sha> --confirm` |
| `coordination-abandoned-claims` | No abandoned `.claim` or `.staging-*` coordination entries | `Found N demonstrably dead claims` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` removes only provably dead ones |
| `runner-coordination-orgPolicy-shape` | `runner.coordination.orgPolicy.dischargeOn` is an array of strings | `... dischargeOn must be an array of strings` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` resets it to the default |
| `coordination-protocol-fixtures-valid` | Coordination protocol definitions validate | `coordination protocol fixtures retired` | info | none |
| `operation-prompt-templates-valid` | Operation prompt templates validate | names the template | you | Fix the named template |
| `coordination-example-requests-valid` | Published coordination example requests validate | `coordination example requests retired` | info | none |
| `shadow-binder-divergence` | Placement shadow-binder divergence is recorded durably | names the divergence | info | Report it |
| `observe-dir-writable` | `.fgos/observe` is writable | names the path | you | Fix directory permissions |
| `observe-friction-migrated` | Legacy friction records are migrated to `.fgos/observe/friction` | `N legacy work.friction record(s) newer than cursor (not migrated) -- run: <host binary> friction migrate --dir <project>` | you | Run the named command. `friction` is a Rust host verb (`.fgos/installation/bin/fgos`, or `FGOS_HOST_BIN`); the Node `fgos` entry has no such verb and no registered fix does it |
| `observe-host-resolvable` | The Rust host resolves and supports observe commands | `host binary unavailable (FGOS_HOST_BIN unset and no active installation ...)` | you | `fgctl repair` |

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 4.6. Docs and generated projections

| Id | Checks | Typical failing message | Who | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enduser-docs-index-stale` | `docs/enduser-docs-index.json` covers every end-user doc | `N/M docs in the index` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` (same as `fgos docs-index`) |
| `decision-index-stale` | `docs/decisions/index.md` matches the logged decisions | `... is stale` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `doc-registry-stale` | `docs/doc-registry.md` and `.json` are current | `docs/doc-registry.md or docs/doc-registry.json is stale -- run fgos doc-registry` | tool | `fgos doctor --fix` |
| `doc-alias-broken` | Doc aliases point to valid paths | names the alias | you | Fix the alias target |
| `doc-active-duplicate` | No duplicate active docs for one topic and role | names the pair | you | Retire one |
| `doc-current-path-missing` | A doc's `currentPath` exists at HEAD | `1 doc(s) with currentPath absent at HEAD` | you | Restore the file or update the registry entry |
| `doc-source-unreachable` | Source capture linkage is reachable | names the capture | you | Repair the link |
| `doc-near-duplicate` | No near-duplicate authoritative claims | names the pair | you | Merge the docs |
| `doc-provisional-aged` | No provisional doc is past its age limit | names the doc | you | Promote or retire it |
| `doc-topic-oversized` | No topic is over its size ceiling | names the topic | you | Split the topic |
| `doc-role-underused` | Role usage frequency | `362 roles used by single doc ...` | info | none |

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.title: 5.2. Pools and independence
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sample: 5.2. Pools and independence
ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 5.2. Pools and independence
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 5.2. Pools and independence

A Workflow unit names a capability, for example `nominal-group:generate`. The
runner picks executors from that capability's pool in
`<project>/.fgos/config.json`:

```json
"runner": { "capabilities": { "nominal-group:generate": {
  "prefer": [
    { "executor": "claude" },
    { "executor": "xai", "invocation": "omp-herdr" },
    { "executor": "openai" },
    { "executor": "glm", "invocation": "pi-cli-bwrap" }
  ] } } }
```

A reviewed unit's checkers must come from a different provider family than the
producer (hard rule). A panel only prefers a different family per seat:
`bind()` gives each seat the first family in `prefer` order that no earlier seat
uses, then the least used one, so a panel may have more seats than the pool has
families and some seats share a family (the run's `unit-summary.json` lists them
under `sharedFamilies`). The `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` check fails
on a reviewed unit that lacks a second family and only notes, without failing,
which panel seats would share a family.
"Runnable" here means what the binder can place (allow-list, confinement,
herdr). It does not see a family whose CLI is blocked on a trust prompt or whose
account is out of quota, so a green pool check is not enough on its own.

Edit the `prefer` list of every capability the Workflow uses (`fgos doctor`
lists them), keeping at least one more family than the largest panel.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.title: 5.3. Trust in every agent CLI home
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sample: 5.3. Trust in every agent CLI home
ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 5.3. Trust in every agent CLI home
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 5.3. Trust in every agent CLI home

Each agent CLI keeps its own record of which folders a human has vouched for.
A fresh worktree is a path none of them has seen; fgOS pre-trusts its own
worktrees for claude **only when the repo root is already trusted by you**
(trust is derived, never invented). For codex and agy fgOS does not write at
all. A missing entry stops the agent at a "Trust this folder?" dialog.

| CLI | Where the trust lives | What you do once per project |
|---|---|---|
| claude | `~/.claude.json`, `projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` | Start `claude` in the project root and accept the folder-trust dialog |
| codex | `config.toml` in each codex home an executor uses (for example `~/.codex-x/config.toml`; the path is named by `agent-cli-project-trusted`) | Add `[projects."/abs/path/to/project"]` and under it `trust_level = "trusted"` |
| agy | `.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` in each agy sub-HOME | Add `"/abs/path/to/project"` to the `trustedWorkspaces` array |

Use the exact root the check prints. If you use several codex homes or agy
sub-HOMEs (one per account), repeat for each: the check lists them all.
`agent-cli-project-trusted` verifies codex and agy; claude trust has no doctor
check beyond `trust-store-readable`, so open it once yourself.

### 5.4. Run from inside the project

Run `fgos workflow start ...` (and `workflow status`, `answer`, `resume`) from
the project's root, using the project's own installed `fgos`
(`.fgos/installation/bin/fgos`, or the `fgos` on your `PATH` that resolves to
it). Do not run another checkout's `bin/fgos.mjs` from a different directory with
`--dir /path/to/project`. `--dir` only selects which `.fgos/` store is read and
written; it does not make the project's own configuration, hooks and paths the
ones in force, so a run started that way can silently mix two trees.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sample: 6.1. Start, then watch
ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 6.1. Start, then watch
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 6.1. Start, then watch

```bash
fgos workflow start <workflow-id> --request "<what you want>"
```

`start` returns at once with the run id and a `detached` block (`pid`,
`logPath`, `statusCommand`); a detached `fgos workflow resume <id> --foreground`
does the work. Add `--foreground` to keep it in your terminal until it
completes, fails or parks.

```bash
fgos workflow status <run-id>
```

`status` shows the run's state per step, any open question, and an `advance`
block: `running` (is the detached process alive), `pid`, `logPath`
(`.fgos/workflow-runs/<run-id>/advance.log`), the last log lines while the run
is not completed, and a `hint` when the run says `running`, nothing is advancing
and nothing was recorded for a while. In that case continue it with
`fgos workflow resume <run-id>`.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text: ### 6.3. The outcome `blocked`
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 6.3. The outcome `blocked`

`blocked` means the agent stopped at something only a person can answer, for
example a "Trust this folder?" dialog. The failure text ends with:
"Answer the prompt in the pane, or grant trust for this project in the agent's
own home, then run again." Concretely:

1. Open `visibility.json` of the failing round. A `trustSeedFailed` value names
   the agent home and says the project root "is not itself trusted ... so there
   is nothing to derive trust from": trust is missing, fix it as in 5.3.
2. Open `herdr-diagnosis.json` and read `detectionScreen` to see the actual
   dialog. If it is not a trust prompt (a login, a quota screen), solve that in
   the agent CLI.
3. If the pane is still open (the failure text says "Pane ... is left open"),
   you can answer it there, but the run has already ended as failed. Grant trust
   and start the run again; a run does not retry itself past a blocked outcome.
4. Re-run `fgos doctor`: `agent-cli-project-trusted` should now be green.

ancestry: How to install fgOS in a project and use fgos doctor
docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.text:
1. Open `visibility.json` of the failing round. A `trustSeedFailed` value names
   the agent home and says the project root "is not itself trusted ... so there
   is nothing to derive trust from": trust is missing, fix it as in 5.3.
2. Open `herdr-diagnosis.json` and read `detectionScreen` to see the actual
   dialog. If it is not a trust prompt (a login, a quota screen), solve that in
   the agent CLI.
3. If the pane is still open (the failure text says "Pane ... is left open"),
   you can answer it there, but the run has already ended as failed. Grant trust
   and start the run again; a run does not retry itself past a blocked outcome.
4. Re-run `fgos doctor`: `agent-cli-project-trusted` should now be green.

docs/how-to/install-fgos-in-a-project-an.sectionText:
### 6.4. Other failures

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Step refused with `policy-refusal ... violates independence requirement against [...]` | A `reviewed` checker has no provider family different from the producer's (a panel never refuses for this) | Add a family to the pool (5.2); the producer already ran |
| `execution-timeout` after a long wait | An agent looped or stalled. A busy stream is not treated as idle | Read the round's `stdout.log` and `herdr-diagnosis.json`; consider a different executor in the pool |
| `parked` with an open question | A human gate | Answer: `fgos workflow answer <run-id> --step <step-id> --answer "<text>"`; the run continues |
| `status` says `running`, no progress, `advance.running` false | Detached advance died | `fgos workflow resume <run-id>` |
| Run not found | Wrong project or you ran with a mismatched `--dir` | Run from inside the project (5.4) |
| Everything runs but the agents cannot start | Account not logged in, or provider quarantine | `confined-pane-accounts`, `provider-capacity-state` |

The owner's Q1 answer adopts LockScope option (a) of §5, a Rust-owned scope that receives the caller's held ranks and lease descriptors as explicit, kernel-verifiable parameters; this is B's `heldRanks` made kernel-verifiable, never a bitmap. The reachability pin is installed and read back in prepare, **before** the single-ref target CAS; a multi-ref `update-ref --stdin` transaction is never treated as crash-atomic (the Git floor proof killed one between ref installs, §4, §10). docs/platform/git/spec.md.title: 1. Purpose and boundary
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sample: 1. Purpose and boundary
docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 1. Purpose and boundary
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 1. Purpose and boundary

Git decides what Git state exists, performs typed authorized mutations, and reconciles their interrupted effects. Rust is the live core now; Node transports typed inputs/results and owns no Git policy. There is no public `git(args)` port and no dual-run writer. Workflow, Execution Core, Work, business workflows, setup and Event Store are consumers, not parallel Git cores.

Git owns local object/ref/index/worktree mutations, worktree registration, the local side of fetch/push, and operation recovery. It owns neither business approval nor Work lifecycle, claim/state transaction, reducer, event envelope/union, seal schema, coverage or consumer cache. Holder-lock owns locks/fences; Process owns containment/signals; Session Identity owns writer identity. A read-only request never silently commits, builds, creates a worktree, configures a remote or repairs a repo.

**Projects without Git.** A read-only Unit needs no RepoHandle. When the directory is not a repository, Inspect returns the typed result `notARepository` and Git never turns the absence of a repository into a workflow error; whether a consumer (for example a business workflow, mission #2) proceeds without one is the consumer's decision. A mutation still requires a validated repository.

Required component-boundary row on acceptance: **Git — foundation; owns repository facts, typed Git operations and recovery WAL; consumers Workflow/Execution/Work/Event Store/setup; dependencies holder-lock/process/session-identity; no consumer imports.** Remove “pure git integration” from Workflow's ownership. The signing bundle (2026-10-18) installed this row in `docs/platform/component-boundary.md` and removed “pure git integration” from the Workflow row.

| Mutation layer | Owner / success boundary |
|---|---|
| Local objects/refs | Git; expected-old publication says nothing about checkout or network |
| Local index/worktree/admin | Git; scoped commit/sync/land/restore/create/remove/relocate |
| Remote send/receive | Git transport port; explicit ref mapping and separate remote acknowledgement |
| GitHub API merge | GitHub adapter under consumer authorization; never a local land and never a policy bypass |

A network failure cannot undo local success. API timeout is outcome-unknown until queried; do not blindly issue another merge. GitHub transport must retain consumer approval/Iron Law and record the actual merge commit. This spec authorizes no external send by itself.

Git never imports a consumer. Verify/build/npm/`worktreeSetup.commands` are **not** Git operations (G-030/G-031). Execution provisions after `worktree-create` returns, **outside every Git lock**: the `fgos worktree create` verb runs the dependency install and `worktreeSetup.commands` from its use case, after the Git port has returned. Git may spawn only `git` (plus Process containment of those children). Consumer verification evidence is bound by digest; Git does not claim tests ran.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 2. Shared entities and outcomes
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 2. Shared entities and outcomes

| Entity | Contract |
|---|---|
| RepoHandle | Validated canonical common-dir and trusted main/root identity/topology; never worker `.git` authority |
| WorktreeHandle | Registered gitdir/backlink, canonical path, branch/detached OID, creation identity; revalidated at mutation |
| Oid | Full object-format-aware identifier; validated commit/tree/blob type, no fixed SHA-1 assumption |
| RefName / ExpectedTip | Full validated namespace-qualified **direct** ref; expected `Absent` or exact OID, never wildcard absence. Symbolic refs are refused in owned and mirror namespaces (C1). |
| Scope | Canonical RUL84 entries, matcher version and explicitly expanded generated grants |
| Custody token | The existing `dispatch-cwd` lease (rank 30) on the worktree, held by Execution and extended across the runner commit (owner decision Q2, section 6). Git **validates** the lease descriptor by kernel check and fails closed when it is missing or stale; it does not mint a second lock and there is no Git `Custody` entity. A text session/writer id is not custody. |
| Candidate | Immutable source/target OIDs, exact result tree, parent/mode, **policy evidence digest**, pin |
| OperationId | Repo-scoped idempotency key bound to kind, repo identity, **canonical resource set**, expected values and authority domain; same id with different request digest refused; same id must not bind two disjoint resource sets |
| Receipt | Structured effect receipt (below). Operational evidence, not a consumer event |

Receipt (panelist 1 / C3) — effect is not completion:

```text
operationId, requestDigest,
localEffect {expected, publishedOid?, observedTip, publicationState},
checkout {notApplicable | pending | reconciled | recoveryRequired},
durability {processCrash | stableMedia, capabilityEvidence},
remote {notRequested | acknowledged | unknown | rejected},
consumerSettlement {notOwnedByGit},
attribution {thisInvocationWonCas | effectObservedOnly | uncertain}
```

`publicationState` distinguishes “currently at candidate” from “this invocation's CAS was observed successful.” Seeing `ref == next` after a crash proves the desired state exists; it does **not** prove which actor installed it. Do not manufacture writer attribution from equality. ABA (target returned to expected after a possible successful CAS) does not justify generic retry: a target CAS whose outcome is unknown is never reissued (§10 TargetAttempt rule). The CAS winner is defined per attempt recorded in the WAL, not by OID value over history: exact-old CAS gives at most one successful state-changing CAS per resource within one uninterrupted expected-state generation, and two CASes from the same expected OID across an ABA are both correct Git semantics. OID equality never identifies a generation; per-operation at-most-once is a WAL property, not a CAS property.

Results distinguish `unchanged`, `created`, `committed`, `landed`, `conflicted-open`, `conflict-aborted`, `busy`, `stale`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `published-checkout-pending`, `committed-but-contract-violation`, `remote-outcome-unknown`, `recovery-required`, `abandonedBeforeAttempt` (terminal, pre-attempt PublicationCas, ScopedCommit, Sync or Land, §10 rule 4b: no TargetAttempt, so no target effect), `configApproved` (terminal, ConfigChange only, §10 rule 4c: an effect-free re-approval of existing fetch mappings), `superseded` (terminal, PublicationCas only, §10 rule 4a: a record-only outcome that says nothing about whether the old CAS ran). Include operation id, typed cause, retryability, actual effect/OIDs, exit/signal and bounded redacted stderr. An ancestry query returns yes/no/error; path-at-revision present/absent/error. Corruption, permission and unknown protocol never become “absent”. An ancestry walk that crosses a shallow boundary returns `shallow-history-incomplete` (an error, never “no”), even when both endpoint objects are present: the Git floor proof saw `merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 1 for a true parent after the parent was fetched into a shallow clone. Endpoint presence is not traversal completeness, and cleanup (§11) never treats such an answer as delivery proof. Cancellation after CAS reports the published effect. Local commit, reconciled checkout, remote ack and durable consumer settlement are separate facts.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 3. Typed operations
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 3. Typed operations

All mutations require operation id, validated repository, writer and **declared resource set + existing authority**. No option-bag escape to raw Git args. Reads are bounded/paginated and do not repair. Doctor never mutates.

| Port | Operations and guarantees |
|---|---|
| Inspect | resolveRepo/Ref, status, diff, ancestry, readObjects, pathsAtRevision (batched), listWorktrees, compareContent, snapshotWrites; explicit unknown/error and byte-safe paths; every Inspect call runs with optional locks off (`--no-optional-locks`), because `status` otherwise refreshes the index under `index.lock` |
| Refs | ensureBranch, advanceRef, deleteRef, fastForwardCheckedOut; exact-old CAS, never blind `branch -D`. Exact-old CAS does **not** protect a checked-out branch (`update-ref -d` deleted the current branch in the Git floor proof, and the V-CAS re-check deleted a branch that a worktree registered after the snapshot had checked out): every Refs mutation of `refs/heads/*` takes worktree-admin 40 (§5), and under that one hold revalidates every registered checkout (main and linked; a symbolic HEAD to an unborn name counts as checked out), performs the exact-old CAS, reads back the ref and the registered checkouts, and only then releases 40, so no fgOS worktree registration can come between the check and the effect. An earlier snapshot of checkout membership protects nothing. An in-use ref is refused. No typed operation switches the branch of an existing checkout; one added later takes 40 first. A switch by raw Git or a worker is outside the concurrency guarantee (§9) and is reported as `recovery-required` when that read-back sees it. The one exception is `fastForwardCheckedOut(branch, expectedOld, next)`: fast-forward only, exact-old CAS, the branch is checked out only in a worktree whose verified `dispatch-cwd` lease the caller holds, that checkout is clean, and its tree is updated under that custody; anything else is refused |
| Worktree | create, createDetached, relocate, remove, inspectOrphans, repairRegistration; one admin door, no rm-rf fallback. Git returns after registration/strip of worker `.fgos`; provisioning is Execution. |
| ScopedCommit | preflight/commit; foreign index refusal, custody, literal exact selection, postcommit set/tree proof. A tracked file move is a ScopedCommit with both literal paths (old deleted, new added); failure restores both paths to their immediately pre-commit existence, mode and content before any consumer registry update (a producer move already made before commit remains old-absent/new-present); there is no separate file-move operation |
| Sync | start/inspect/continue/abort; pinned target, scoped resolver, operation-owned merge state |
| Land | prepare/publish/recover; immutable candidate, merge or squash, journalled CAS/checkout. Consumer supplies verification evidence. |
| SafeRestore | preview/apply/recover/listSnapshot/extractPath/acknowledge; full locked checks and durable snapshot before destructive effect. `apply` may carry `reapplyLocalDelta`: after the snapshot and the restore to the new tip, the captured local delta is applied to index and tree; a failed reapply leaves the durable snapshot and returns `recovery-required` (replaces `resyncWorktree`'s `reset --hard` + `apply --index`) |
| Checkpoint adapter | checkpointTrackedFiles; detachable, consumer-selected **non-event** tracked payload only |
| RepositoryConfig | publicationFetchMappings(remote), ensureFetchMapping, ensureHooks, removeOwnedHooksConfig; local config, user settings preserved, provenance |
| Remote | fetchRefs, pushRefs, inspectRemote; explicit mapping, no implicit all-refs or default push-config mutation |
| Recovery | inspectOperation, listPending, reconcile; actual disk/ref checks and idempotent results |
| Publication | restricted plumbing; section 4. Event Store is the only production writer of event refs |

Implementation may collapse ports internally; the appendix maps lessons to this surface. Idempotency is required wherever an effect can repeat.

Implementation checkpoint (2026-10-19, dormant): `src/git/refs.mjs` and `remote.mjs` marshal typed requests and explicit held handles, with no subprocess policy in Node. Refs uses worktree-admin 40 through membership revalidation, exact-old no-dereference CAS and read-back, and journals `RefUpdate`/`RefDelete` with a reachability pin and one TargetAttempt. `fastForwardCheckedOut` requires the exact registered worktree's rank-30 lease and a clean fast-forward. Non-event Remote takes literal source/destination pairs (fetch destinations under `refs/remotes/*`, push destinations under `refs/heads/*`), pins the granted remote URL, downloads objects before exact-old local CAS, and records `RemoteFetch`/`RemotePush` with per-target old/new values before TargetAttempt. Lost acknowledgements preserve the attempt and never resend that id. These ports have no production callers yet; unresolved operations preserve evidence and refuse replay. Linux files/reftable and local bare-remote proofs live in `packages/git/rust/tests/refs_remote.rs` and `test/git/{refs,remote,lock-handover}.test.mjs`. Separate-git-dir remains unsupported: inferred linked-cwd discovery requires a main `.git` directory and reciprocal registered admin/backlink, rather than trusting a worker gitfile alone.

2026-10-19 (phase 05 worktree, **not release-ready**): dormant ScopedCommit, non-event main Checkpoint and Sync ports now have Rust implementations and mechanical addon/Node bindings. ScopedCommit records baseline/ref/dirty-content fingerprints, stages literal NUL pathspecs, records a pre-OID TargetAttempt, and checks the actual committed tree and path set after one hook invocation. A contract violation retains the actual OID. Sync journals its pinned target and operation-owned conflict/staged sets, returns a temporary resolver grant, checks conflict markers before staging, and checks both merge parents. The cutover hook delegates to the activated host's protocol-1 `git-grant-check`; that read-only route verifies the inherited main-50 borrower, WAL description binding, unspent TargetAttempt, exact deletion paths, current legacy ref and seal digest. Every cutover also stages the `.fgos/events` fence when it is present as a regular file, replacing the deleted event directory or, in a baseline-only repository, marking the cutover. Linux-x64 activation now requires the native addon to declare `git-wal-v1`; old manifests still deserialize for a named refusal. Phase-05 unit 2 carries a real pre-open acquisition reach floor through the private Node handle and opaque loan, and the release/dev-host/test addon producer emits its platform capabilities. Sync records a durable `sync-commit-attempt` (prepared tree) immediately before invoking commit and refuses an uncertain attempt on resume, even when HEAD matches; its resulting ref is synced before the outcome. ScopedCommit and Sync receipt replay derive the actual committed path set from the immutable commit, preserving hook contract violations. Parent-death barriers and genuine temporary hook indexes have Linux fixture evidence. Unit 3 restores declared producer bytes from a transaction-local pre-staging snapshot after an observed rejection with unchanged HEAD, including both move paths, clean declared files, symlinks and modes; the initially empty index is restored even when the hook staged extra paths. Uncertain/crashed attempts retain the WAL and refuse replay rather than guessing rollback. Adopted setsid holders use the holder-lock descriptor rule below. Installed-release main cutover and unrestricted host/cross-platform acceptance remain outstanding. See [unit-2 report](../../../plans/reports/phase-lead-261019-1654-git-p05-u2-handover-reach-and-capability.md). The Node matcher and existing production commit/sync adapters remain for the planned phase-07 switch; no dormant port is an authorization to switch callers early.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): RepositoryConfig is the single source for publication fetch mappings. Event Store and Node setup/doctor read the Rust policy through the existing crate/addon boundary. The legacy mapping is `+refs/fgos/legacy*:refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy*`: Git permits an absent wildcard source, including before the cutover, and the empty suffix maps `refs/fgos/legacy` to exactly `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy`. ensureFetchMapping replaces an installed old exact legacy mapping in the same journaled, native-config-lock-protected update, including when both forms exist; unrelated config and push settings remain untouched. Setup/doctor use `eventStore.remote` (project over global, registered setup default `origin`), and also detect and migrate obsolete exact mappings on `origin` when the configured remote differs. `obsolete_legacy_fetch_mapping` owns the obsolete form for every consumer; callers do not infer it by policy-list index. The wildcard reserves all `refs/fgos/legacy?*` names (any nonempty suffix): writers must never create them. Doctor reports any corresponding `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy?*` mirrors, with source/mirror cleanup guidance; it never deletes these refs automatically.

2026-10-19 (review fixes): Untrusted repository URL rewrites (`url.*`, including `insteadOf` and `pushInsteadOf`) refuse before invocation. Remote overrides generic HTTP proxy, TLS verification, extra headers and redirect policy with safe values, and refuses other repository-local HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, credential, protocol and proxy overrides, including URL-scoped HTTP settings; trusted global transport configuration remains outside this repository boundary. Trust is determined by `git config --show-scope`: only system/global/command scopes are trusted; local/worktree and any unknown scope are untrusted, regardless of origin path spelling. Both the trusted main checkout and a linked handle’s worktree configuration are checked. Doctor’s `git-transport-config` reports refusing settings, including actions/checkout’s local `http.<url>.extraheader`; CI uses `persist-credentials: false` plus a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. Doctor never migrates secrets. Trusted global credential helpers remain available to Remote/Publication; preflight still refuses repository-local helpers, and the driver still scrubs inherited `GIT_*` overrides. SSH URLs may select a username (`ssh://git@host/path`); password/userinfo credentials are refused. Push uses `--atomic`, never forces, and classifies every destination from post-transfer observations; all unchanged destinations establish rejection, mixed observations remain unknown. Fetch refreshes remote-tracking refs with Git's default forced-update semantics, protected by exact-old no-dereference CAS; ancestry is not required. All destinations are checked before the first install. A stale destination or failed install with no local effect closes with a terminal not-acknowledged Transfer and per-target observations, without a pending operation id; readable partial installs close as unknown with observations. Unreadable outcomes retain recovery evidence and never replay. A failed fetch CAS does not stop the remaining destination installs; the final observations cover all destinations. A server without atomic push support produces a terminal Rejected outcome; there is no non-atomic fallback.

`fastForwardCheckedOut` refuses the trusted main checkout. Membership includes rebase-merge/rebase-apply `head-name` and `BISECT_START`; an ordinary user worktree lock does not make registration uncertain, while `locked initializing` does. Doctor `git-worktree-recovery` classifies a lock for inspection only (2026-10-19): a lock whose reason names `pid <N>` where process N is live and started no later than the lock file (pid plus start time, so a reused pid does not count) is `locked-by-live-process`, advisory like `dirty-or-stale-checkout-preserved`; a lock naming a dead, reused or unparseable owner stays `locked-registration` and fails the row. The reason text is read only for that pid token, never as authority for anything else, and nothing is unlocked or repaired. An explicit ignored-path/incoming-tree collision check preserves ignored content (Git 2.53 dry-run alone did not refuse the measured replacement). After index refresh, a dry-run two-tree `read-tree -m -n -u` must pass before TargetAttempt. A failed ref write which still observes the expected old tip is a write failure with recovery evidence, never a claimed CAS loss. RemoteFetch/RemotePush are the sole transfer WAL kinds, with explicit target old/new values for both Publication and non-event Remote; Publication retains its authority, expected/next and no-resend recovery rules. Historical Publication records without target detail deserialize with an empty target list for conservative recovery; all new writers emit the targets field and non-event transfers require a complete target set.

2026-10-19 (phase 03): Worktree uses the existing Rust LockScope, worktree-admin 40, Inspect topology, hardened driver, WAL admission/TargetAttempt and reachability pins. One hold spans identity/custody/status/proof checks and remove/move. Git children borrow admin authority; the caller's verified custody description stays pinned in the seeded scope until return. Remove preserves staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored and reappearing worker-state bytes, native locks, live cwd and unknown process facts; a process that exits during the cwd scan is re-observed through Process before treating its missing cwd as clear. A successful create strips worker `.fgos`; intentionally absent tracked state paths are marked skip-worktree in the new checkout's index, so later cleanup does not need an exemption for dirty paths. No provisioning callback runs in Git. Detached session allocation owns an `mkdtemp` directory and only attempts an empty-directory rollback before registration; registered cleanup always goes through non-force Git removal.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): A tracked, clean `.fgos` with no skip-worktree entries is not reappearing worker state and does not prevent Worktree removal or relocation.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 host gate): An unreadable cwd does not refuse remove or relocate; live same-user or unknown-owner processes with unreadable cwds produce a stderr warning naming pid and comm. A readable cwd inside or below the checkout still refuses. The caller's verified dispatch-cwd lease and refusal of another holder's lease cover fgOS producers; status checks preserve dirty or uncertain trees. Unreadability alone is not evidence that a process occupies this checkout.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 review): Allocation inside the trusted main checkout (including ignored `.claude/worktrees`) is supported; equal/ancestor paths, the common Git directory and nesting in linked checkouts remain refused. Readable cwd facts from any user protect a checkout; unreadable cwd facts are judged only for the effective user or unknown ownership. Privileged actors and unreadable foreign-user processes are outside this guarantee, so shared cross-user checkout custody is not certified. Same-user unreadability is advisory (see the host-gate policy below). Remove/move preflight refuses user locks and submodules and repeats custody/cwd checks immediately before TargetAttempt and the Git call. Removal additionally requires `deliveredTo` reachable from a surviving named non-`refs/fgos` ref; a detached tip alone is not delivery. Ignored bytes remain protected; ignored-directory inspection is collapsed with `--directory` and bounded by the Inspect output ceiling. Doctor reports preserved dirty/stale checkouts as advisory; pending operations, missing/locked registrations and partial/untrusted admin entries fail the row.

Under worktree-admin, after an attempted Git refusal or during repair, observable non-effects settle as terminal `Worktree { completed: false, details }` with the checked paths/registration observations, then release the candidate pin. Create requires absent registration and absent or empty owned destination; move requires absent destination plus unchanged admin identity, reciprocal source backlink and expected tip; remove requires that unchanged source state. This is record-only reconciliation under §10 rule 4, never a repeated attempt or a claim that an attempted operation was abandoned before attempt (§10 rule 4b). A replay of a false outcome returns a terminal refusal. Ambiguous residue remains pending and preserved.


Worktree WAL kinds bind canonical paths and registration names; move/remove additionally bind the admin directory's `dev:ino`, and remove binds the consumer's expected tip, delivery target and evidence digest. An established id is replayed without repeating its effect; pending attempts retain evidence. Recovery repairs a move only at its recorded destination and checks that destination's gitfile. An initializing create lock requires its own attempted WAL record, matching registration, branch and tip; a partial or dirty checkout stays preserved. Prune accepts only attempted WorktreeRemove evidence, a missing recorded checkout, the same admin inode and a matching backlink (or a partially removed backlink); it removes only the validated Git admin remainder, preserving unknown files, symlinks and native locks. It never invokes global prune or acquires custody. Four Linux x86_64 crash fixtures kill actual Git at ptrace syscall barriers; power-loss durability is not claimed.

`fgos worktree create <path> [--branch <name> | --detach] [--base <ref>] [--json]` is available now under the owner's plan Q2 answer of 2026-10-18. Without a branch it creates a detached checkout. After the port returns, the verb provisions the new checkout through the runner's own helpers (`provisionDependencies`, then the project's `worktreeSetup.commands` with `FGOS_REPO_ROOT` set to the main checkout), outside every Git lock; a failing setup command fails the verb and leaves the created checkout in place. This is the one door: workflow and `fgos run --worktree` worktrees are made by this verb or by the runner's own creators, which already provision. Base accepts a full OID, HEAD or a literal branch/tag/remote ref. `fgos worktree remove <path> --delivered-to <ref> [--json]` (owner-approved 2026-10-20) wires the port's guarded remove: it resolves the worktree's current tip as `expectedTip`, resolves the delivery target (branch name, full ref or object id) to `deliveredTo`, and passes the sha256 of the delivery statement `{path, expectedTip, deliveredTo: {ref, oid}}` as `evidenceDigest`. The port refuses a dirty checkout, a live process, preserved worker state, a tip that is not an ancestor of (or equal to) `deliveredTo`, or a `deliveredTo` no non-internal ref contains; its error code and message surface unchanged and there is no force flag. Other production Worktree callers migrate together in phase 07. `git-worktree-recovery` reads raw admin entries (including partial entries omitted by Git listing), dirty/stale checkouts and pending Worktree WAL records without repairing; phase 04 adds its producing-custody row to this same diagnostic.

| ScopedCommit | preflight/commit; foreign index refusal, custody, literal exact selection, postcommit set/tree proof. A tracked file move is a ScopedCommit with both literal paths (old deleted, new added); failure restores both paths to their immediately pre-commit existence, mode and content before any consumer registry update (a producer move already made before commit remains old-absent/new-present); there is no separate file-move operation |
| Sync | start/inspect/continue/abort; pinned target, scoped resolver, operation-owned merge state |
| Land | prepare/publish/recover; immutable candidate, merge or squash, journalled CAS/checkout. Consumer supplies verification evidence. |
| SafeRestore | preview/apply/recover/listSnapshot/extractPath/acknowledge; full locked checks and durable snapshot before destructive effect. `apply` may carry `reapplyLocalDelta`: after the snapshot and the restore to the new tip, the captured local delta is applied to index and tree; a failed reapply leaves the durable snapshot and returns `recovery-required` (replaces `resyncWorktree`'s `reset --hard` + `apply --index`) |
| Checkpoint adapter | checkpointTrackedFiles; detachable, consumer-selected **non-event** tracked payload only |
| RepositoryConfig | publicationFetchMappings(remote), ensureFetchMapping, ensureHooks, removeOwnedHooksConfig; local config, user settings preserved, provenance |
| Remote | fetchRefs, pushRefs, inspectRemote; explicit mapping, no implicit all-refs or default push-config mutation |
| Recovery | inspectOperation, listPending, reconcile; actual disk/ref checks and idempotent results |
| Publication | restricted plumbing; section 4. Event Store is the only production writer of event refs |

Trust is determined by `git config --show-scope`: only system/global/command scopes are trusted; local/worktree and any unknown scope are untrusted, regardless of origin path spelling. Both the trusted main checkout and a linked handle’s worktree configuration are checked. Doctor’s `git-transport-config` reports refusing settings, including actions/checkout’s local `http.<url>.extraheader`; CI uses `persist-credentials: false` plus a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. Doctor never migrates secrets. Trusted global credential helpers remain available to Remote/Publication; preflight still refuses repository-local helpers, and the driver still scrubs inherited `GIT_*` overrides. SSH URLs may select a username (`ssh://git@host/path`); password/userinfo credentials are refused. Push uses `--atomic`, never forces, and classifies every destination from post-transfer observations; all unchanged destinations establish rejection, mixed observations remain unknown. Fetch refreshes remote-tracking refs with Git's default forced-update semantics, protected by exact-old no-dereference CAS; ancestry is not required. All destinations are checked before the first install. A stale destination or failed install with no local effect closes with a terminal not-acknowledged Transfer and per-target observations, without a pending operation id; readable partial installs close as unknown with observations. Unreadable outcomes retain recovery evidence and never replay. A failed fetch CAS does not stop the remaining destination installs; the final observations cover all destinations. A server without atomic push support produces a terminal Rejected outcome; there is no non-atomic fallback.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ### Dormant Recovery and GitHub adapter contract (phase 06 units 9–13)
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
### Dormant Recovery and GitHub adapter contract (phase 06 units 9–13)

`createGitRecovery(options)` exposes `inspectOperation({operationId})`,
`listPending({bound?})`, and `reconcile({operationId}, held?)`. Inspection
returns the request digest, payload kind, terminal state and retained intent;
compacted operations return their retained request digest and terminal outcome.
Pending scans return `{operations, complete}`; corruption refuses by operation
id rather than silently omitting evidence. Unsupported payload variants refuse
with their variant name through WAL decoding. Reconciliation delegates to the
owning port and returns its Rust result (a receipt for Land/Publication, an
outcome for ref/transfer/ScopedCommit, the existing result for Restore/Sync,
and inspection after Worktree repair). A compacted operation returns its
terminal WAL outcome without introducing any new effect. Recovery holds are
released before returning to consumer settlement; no consumer state is written.

ConfigChange reconciliation delegates to the existing config recovery under
repo-config 80, without acquiring the peer-rank recovery leaf. This resource
authority excludes fgOS config writers and recoverers; native config.lock
excludes ordinary Git writers. Caller loans are refused on ConfigChange rather
than silently dropped. The interrupted-operation matrix covers all twelve
payload kinds at durable Intent in both recovery orders; additional ref/transfer
rows cover pin installation, TargetAttempt and observed CAS. Production caller
moves remain for phase 07.

Publication recovery retains its existing event-seal resource authority without
taking the recovery leaf, including live Event Store publish/recover paths.
Other recovery paths take recovery 80 last; it never substitutes for resource
authority. Git reuses the registered recovery lock with
`runDir=<common>/fgos/git`, hence `<common>/fgos/git/locks/recovery.lock`.
Non-event transfers retain their lock-free scope (caller ranks below 60);
worktree-admin belongs only to their observe-only recovery, not transfer admission.

GitHub API merge stays in the GitHub adapter under **consumer authorization**;
Git ports do not grant approval or perform API merges. A merge timeout is
**outcome-unknown until queried**, including the adapter's existing
`blocked` transport result: it does not prove the server declined the merge.
The production adapter queries PR state/merge commit after an unreachable merge
result, returns the observed merged receipt when available, otherwise retains
`blocked` with `reason: outcome-unknown`. A repeated merge call first queries
state and returns an existing MERGED result without sending another request.
The contract test invokes the production merge adapter twice.
Any local mutation the adapter needs must go through the typed Git ports.
Phase 06 adds the timeout-query and MERGED guard to the existing adapter; the phase 07 caller move remains separate.
